articles.title: Russia Hacked Routers to Steal Microsoft Office Tokens
articles.summary: Microsoft just hemorrhaged 167 vulnerabilities including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. Meanwhile Chrome patched its fourth zero-day this year because apparently browsers are just suggestion boxes for attackers now.

articles.title: The Internet Still Works: SmugMug Powers Online Photography
articles.summary: Congress is frantically trying to slap a fresh coat of paint on the surveillance state with their 'Foreign Intelligence Accountability Act' before Section 702 expires. Spoiler alert: it's still mass warrantless spying with a prettier name.

articles.title: Feuding Ransomware Groups Leak Each Other's Data
articles.summary: The NSA's former deputy director finally breaks his silence on the Snowden affair 13 years later, admitting they screwed up royally. Better late than never, but some of us were paying attention when it mattered.

articles.title: CIA Ran MK-ULTRA Experiments on Prisoners of War in U.S. Custody, Declassified Docs Confirm
articles.summary: Four Democrats hold the keys to whether Trump gets his domestic spying wet dream renewed. Because nothing says 'resistance' like handing fascists the tools to spy on everyone without warrants.

articles.title: Don't pay Vect a ransom - your data's likely already wiped out
articles.summary: Freshly declassified docs confirm the CIA ran MK-ULTRA mind control experiments on North Korean POWs in U.S. custody. Your tax dollars at work, turning human beings into lab rats since 1953.

articles.title: Brazilian LofyGang Resurfaces After Three Years With Minecraft LofyStealer Campaign
articles.summary: Researchers found CVE-2026-3854, a critical GitHub RCE flaw that lets authenticated users own servers with a single git push. Because apparently even Microsoft's code repositories are security theater.

articles.title: Anthropic Mythos: Firms with access to model say speed of response, not uncovering flaws, is key
articles.summary: Hugging Face's LeRobot platform is sporting an unpatched critical RCE flaw that screams 'pwn me harder daddy.' 24,000 GitHub stars can't hide the fact that someone forgot to sanitize their inputs.

articles.title: ShinyHunters Leaks Data of Udemy, Zara, 7-Eleven in Salesforce Linked Breach
articles.summary: Medical device giant Medtronic got pwned by ShinyHunters who allegedly made off with 9+ million records. Nothing says 'trust us with your pacemaker' like having your entire customer database yoinked by script kiddies.

articles.title: TeamPCP Supply Chain Campaign: Update 008 - 26-Day Pause Ends with Three Concurrent Compromises (Checkmarx KICS, Bitwarden CLI Cascade, xinference PyPI), CanisterSprawl npm Worm Identified, and Tier 1 Coverage Returns, (Mon, Apr 27th)
articles.summary: ShinyHunters is having a field day leaking Salesforce-connected data from Udemy, Zara, and 7-Eleven. When your CRM becomes everyone's personal shopping list, you know cloud security is working as intended.

articles.title: Daily Hacker News for 2026-04-24
articles.summary: The TeamPCP supply chain campaign resurges after a 26-day nap, hitting Checkmarx, Bitwarden CLI, and spawning the delightfully named 'CanisterSprawl' npm worm. Because apparently our entire development ecosystem is held together with compromised duct tape.
